records.hook_structure: curiosity-gap + age-shock framing: anonymized 'this kid' teaser -> escalating dollar-figure card -> reveal he's still underage/in-school, priming a rags-to-riches insider story

whip-pan/motion-blur cold-open into rapid identity-stacking cards (name -> title -> logo) that establish authority before any claim is spoken, functioning as a credibility hook rather than a question-based curiosity gap

direct how-to promise + escalating-stat proof: 'here's how' spoken cold-open immediately paired with a climbing on-screen counter (88→100 'TikToks per hour') to visually dramatize the claim before the tool is even named

quality-shaming setup -> personal-solution reveal: 'posted on TikTok/Instagram looks trash' problem-framing cuts into 'I have the solution for you' with a day-count series stamp, front-loaded with rapid word-by-word kinetic text to hold attention before any explanation is given

problem-cost hook: on-screen word-build captions state the pain ('stop editing manually' / 'your captions') while a fake digital counter spins up to 03:00:00, turning an abstract complaint into a visualized time-cost before the solution is revealed

accusatory curiosity-gap hook: a blunt theft/loss claim ('captions are stealing your editing time') is slapped over a direct-address talking head with zero preamble, building word-by-word to force a read, then the pain is dramatized (tired eyes, every-hour grind) before the twist/payoff of naming the actual tool.

accusatory-callout hook stacked with word-by-word kinetic text: 'IF YOURE NOT MAKING VIDEOS because YOU DONT KNOW HOW TO EDIT' -> reframed as excuse ('EXCUSE = NO GOOD'), baiting viewer identity before pivoting to solution pitch

curiosity-gap product tease: title card 'EDITS' spins in over direct-address claim ('today I'm going to show you how I get clean edits') -> promise is immediately validated by a whip-pan/jump cut to a different room, proving the 'clean edit' claim in real time

meta/self-referential curiosity-gap hook: direct address about the on-screen caption text itself -> reveal twist ('I didn't write a single word') that pivots into a problem/insider framing about generic auto-captions making everyone look the same

reenacted-DM/comment cold-open ('THIS...') interrupted by a hard whip-pan/glitch transition into a stylised promise-card sequence ('WHEN I GOT MADE to your video WITHOUT doing it MANUALLY'), baiting curiosity about a claimed AI shortcut before naming the tool
